- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast modestly to avoid excessive sell-off.  
- Model frequently overestimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) — cap forecast at 1.1x recent peak for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if recent 18-day mean is below 30-day average.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% on day 4+ of sentiment reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses momentum — add 0.3–0.7% upward bias if recent 7-day avg > 30-day avg.
